home.why: Hero is text: LCP follows the head bytes (about 8-9 ms per raw KB in the lab); the home is the heaviest first screen.

me.why: Recruiter page: hero photo plus experience blocks, the numbered layer rail and the folded more-tools block of the full-stack story, and 44 px hit areas; its LCP margin is the thinnest after /experiments/.

experiments.why: Two featured pieces; the CSS of compact cards, pager, sort switch and gallery ships only where it renders.

changelog.why: Release days grouped by kind, 4 days per page (page 1 opens the 2 newest); the flat list was about 130 KB, and the page CSS ships only here. The compact lab-paper banner of the inner pages adds about 2.2 KB of CSS (this page's sheet did not carry the banner styles) and 2.9 KB of HTML. Release of 2026-10-12: html 113000 -> 115800 (measured 115792 on page 2): each new release day pushes the oldest day of page 1 onto page 2.

contact.why: Form page: the lightest shared head, only the site stylesheet plus the form.

subscribe.why: Form page: the site stylesheet plus a small form, no page-specific CSS to speak of.

notes-index.why: Fixed index shell plus 4000 HTML bytes per published note (rows, filter metadata and category/tag links). A 180000 B absolute ceiling requires pagination at larger scales; CSS remains independently bounded.

topic.why: Static topic page /notes/tag/<topic>/: compact paper banner, an intro and compact note rows; no script. Same stylesheet as /notes/. Budget is the measured value rounded up to 100 B, so a new utility or a longer intro shows up.

note.why: Fixed note shell excludes the rendered MDX body, measured between inert template boundaries. Article content has a separate 64 KiB ceiling; CSS, JavaScript and Lighthouse gates remain independent.

result.why: One short card under the compact banner (404, confirm and unsubscribe, es and en): budget is the measured value rounded up to 100 B, so these small pages stay tight.

default.why: Legal pages, subscribe steps, paged or sorted listings: ceiling for anything without its own type.
